Let \(u,v\) be an oriented orthonormal basis of \(L\), where
\[
u=(u_1,u_2,u_3,u_4),\qquad v=(v_1,v_2,v_3,v_4).
\]
In the basis \((u,v)\) of \(L\),
\[
P_L e_i=u_i u+v_i v,
\]
so
\[
A_{ij}=\left|u_i v_j-u_j v_i\right|.
\]
Write
\[
p_{ij}=u_i v_j-u_j v_i.
\]
Since \(u,v\) are orthonormal,
\[
\sum_{i<j}p_{ij}^2=1
\]
by Cauchy-Binet. Also the six \(p_{ij}\) satisfy the Plucker relation
\[
p_{12}p_{34}-p_{13}p_{24}+p_{14}p_{23}=0.
\]

Set
\[
x_{ij}=|p_{ij}|,
\]
and define
\[
t_1=x_{12}x_{34},\qquad t_2=x_{13}x_{24},\qquad t_3=x_{14}x_{23}.
\]
The Plucker relation implies that among \(t_1,t_2,t_3\), one is the sum of the other two. Let the largest be \(M\). Then
\[
t_1+t_2+t_3=2M.
\]
Also
\[
1=\sum_{i<j}x_{ij}^2
\ge 2x_{12}x_{34}+2x_{13}x_{24}+2x_{14}x_{23}
=2(t_1+t_2+t_3)=4M,
\]
so \(M\le \frac14\).

The desired product is
\[
\prod_{i<j}A_{ij}
=\prod_{i<j}x_{ij}
=t_1t_2t_3.
\]
If \(M\) is the largest and the other two terms sum to \(M\), their product is at most \((M/2)^2\). Hence
\[
t_1t_2t_3\le M\left(\frac M2\right)^2=\frac{M^3}{4}
\le \frac{1}{256}.
\]

It remains to show equality is attainable. Take absolute Plucker coordinates
\[
x_{12}=x_{34}=x_{14}=x_{23}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt2},
\qquad
x_{13}=x_{24}=\frac12.
\]
Then
\[
x_{12}x_{34}+x_{14}x_{23}
=\frac18+\frac18
=\frac14
=x_{13}x_{24},
\]
so the Plucker relation can be satisfied, and
\[
\sum_{i<j}x_{ij}^2
=4\cdot \frac18+2\cdot \frac14
=1.
\]
Thus these are the Plucker coordinates of some oriented two-plane \(L\), and the product is
\[
\left(\frac{1}{2\sqrt2}\right)^4\left(\frac12\right)^2
=\frac{1}{256}.
\]

Therefore the maximum possible value is
\[
\boxed{\frac{1}{256}}.
\]
